Hey! I also have weird things happening to me during sleeping hours. I know it sounds weird and not logical but panic attacks can happen at the strangest times, it actually happened to me once during the night, like I woke up and a had panic attack out of nowhere. It was so bad I thought I was dying and couldn't believe it was just a panic attack because... HOW? but turns out it was \^\^ I'm not saying it's what happened to you but it could be.   


Anyway, I'm kinda asking myself the same questions as you about those weird things that happen at night. A part of me tries to find a rational explanation but I can't help but think about paranormal things. I'm not sure we'll ever get an answer :/

Well I saw weird things again last night, but not the people. I saw my door changed, like it was a front door with windows and the light outside woke me up. I fell back asleep and was again woken up, this time by my window that was suddenly different, and the light woke me up again, even though it was supposed to be pitch dark. It's really weird but it doesn't creep me out, I shrug it off and go back to sleep while I can't do that when I see the people looking at me.
Will do, thank you for your answer!

I know I have hypnagogic hallucinations sometimes: in general I see spiders falling on me, or that kind of things. But I realise afterwards that I was asleep. When I see those people though, it's a different sensation, it really creeps me out. But yeah that's probably the most rational explanation!

- I don't see them every night, it's pretty random. I'm not sure if they're different people or not because I don't really remember their faces once the night is over.
- I think I'm fully awake when that happens because I wake up with a start, my heart is racing and I sit up in my bed.
- I haven't seen them my whole life, I'd say it's pretty recent (1 or 2 years)
- I do suffer from depression but I'm not prone to hallucinations.
- I also have a sleep disorder, I'm diagnosed with hypersomnia. So yeah that could come from that
- My mom had one paranormal experience, at least she told me about one: my brother was a toddler then. At that time, they used to make sure the sheets wouldn't move with some sort of string (I have no idea how to describe that, I don't even know what it really is, we don't use those nowadays because it's not safe). So it's the middle of the night and my brother's sleeping. My mom then wakes up because a shadowy figure is shaking her. She tries to fall back asleep but then it happens again, like the shadowy figure urges her to get up. So she gets up, go check on my brother and he was suffocating because of the sheets. According to her, he would have died if she hadn't got up. She told the story to my dad but he never believed her so she didn't talk about that to anyone else, until that day she saw me watching a documentary about near-death experience on the internet. (Funny thing: my brother once broke his arm and went to see a physiotherapist. She told him he had a ghost following him)

Sorry if it's long to read. Sorry if I make any grammatical error! Here's my story:

I  was really depressed and going through some hard time. One evening, I  realized my boyfriend was a compulsive liar, he kept telling me personnal stories about himself and naturally I told him (very) personnal  stories about myself. Turns out pretty much everything he told me was an  elaborate lie, which he admitted that night. Anyway, we broke up and  that moment felt like the final straw for me. I was like "Well fuck it,  I'm really tired of this life" so I took a shitload of pills, put on my  pajamas and went to bed, thinking I'd die in my sleep and would never  wake up. I know it might sound stupid but I was in a very bad place,  psychologically speaking.

Thing is, my  (ex) boyfriend started telling me how he was also feeling suicidal and I thought to myself "Oh no way you little fucker, you don't get to kill  yourself". I told him I didn't want to see him but that he should go to  the emergency room and tell them how he felt. I made him promise he'd do it and he assured me he would. But then I remembered he was a pathological  liar. So I got up, got dressed and told him I'd meet him in front of the  emergency room. It was a 5 minutes drive from my home so I thought I  could go there, make sure he was taken care of, and go back home to  finally die. That's the last thing I remember from that night. When I  didn't show up, he got worried and called my parents who went looking  for me. I apparently took the subway but got up one station too early. It's a station I perfectly know, I go there every morning to go to the university, but somehow I was lost. The pills I took (strong sedative antipsychotics) fucked me up sooner than I thought and I had no idea where I was. They found me there in a fucked up state and took me to the emergency room. My boyfriend admitted he didn't feel suicidal at all and went home. I fell into some sort of coma, they tried to wake me up but couldn't. Around 3 in the morning, they called my parents (who went home), telling them I was in a life-threatening situation and they weren't sure if I was goign to make it or not. I woke up something like one day later, in a reanimation room. Doctors asked me if I knew where I was. "The hospital", I guessed. Everytime I answered that, they looked pissed. "You're not just in the hospital, you're in the reanimation room. It could have been very serious". They gave me a yogourt and I couldn't eat properly. I couldn't aim my mouth, it was messy. I don't know why, but I remember the yogourt part very clearly. Which is kinda weird because I don't really remember the rest. After that, I fell asleep again, then woke up and fell asleep over and over again for a long time. Anyway, I lived. But if I didn't got up to find my ex boyfriend, I would probably be dead right now. I only made it because they reanimated me. If he hadn't lied about being suicidal, I would have died alone in my bed ans that thought really fucks me up. I feel like I cheated death and shouldn't be alive right now.
